summary: The target-only mode cannot reach its input: it expands to `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_noraceblock0.dta`, while the generated and scored file is `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`. After correcting that, preserve the batch log because `capture log close` prevents Run-Stata from observing its completion marker; target-mode intermediate outputs also need isolation.

findings.title: Target mode constructs the wrong link filename and stops before producing figures
findings.what_the_code_does: When `FIG_NEWLINKS` is `mltgt1940`, the code assigns `local newv "$FIG_NEWLINKS"` and requests `link1930_1940_`newv'_noraceblock0.dta`, yielding `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_noraceblock0.dta`. The producer instead constructs version `_mltgt1940` and then appends `_cleaned`, and the scorer explicitly opens `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`.
findings.why_it_matters: The target-mode merge encounters a nonexistent using file and terminates before writing `temp_tgt.dta`, the target PDFs, or substantive replication numbers. Because `repnum open` occurs earlier, it can also leave a header-only target results file that looks like an attempted output.
findings.how_to_check: Run `Test-Path 'D:/SNU ECON Dropbox/sam hwang/enum_date/DATA/INTERMEDIATE/link1930_1940_mltgt1940_noraceblock0.dta'` and the same command with `mltgt1940_cleaned`; only the latter should exist. Alternatively, run `confirm file` on both names in Stata.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the accepted switch value as `mltgt1940`, but set the target link stem to `mltgt1940_cleaned` before interpolating it into the path, for example with a separate `local newv "mltgt1940_cleaned"`. Preserve `true_cleaned` in the default branch.

findings.title: The analysis closes the batch log that Run-Stata uses to detect completion
findings.what_the_code_does: The documented runner starts Stata in batch mode and recognizes completion only when its outer wrapper writes `RUN-STATA-RC:` into `_run__figs_tgt_run.log`. The first inner command is `capture log close`, which closes that unnamed batch log; the script later opens and closes a different unnamed log but never reopens the batch log before the outer wrapper displays the marker.
findings.why_it_matters: The Stata work may finish or fail, but Run-Stata cannot observe either outcome. With `/b` still waiting after execution, the PowerShell runner can wait for its 600-minute default timeout and then kill Stata, reporting a timeout instead of the real return code.
findings.how_to_check: Run `powershell -File replication/Run-Stata.ps1 -DoFile MATCHING/_figs_tgt_run.do -TimeoutMinutes 1` with the current path error present. Inspect `MATCHING/_figs_tgt_run.log`; it will lack `RUN-STATA-RC:` after the inner `log close`, so the runner times out rather than reporting the immediate Stata error.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the batch log. Remove the blanket `capture log close`, and give the pipe-delimited socio-demographic log a name via `log using ..., name(...)`; use the same name for `log on`, `log off`, and `log close` so it can coexist with Run-Stata's unnamed batch log.

findings.title: Target mode still replaces shared graph and log intermediates without the target suffix
findings.what_the_code_does: Final exports interpolate `sfx`, but the graph saves remain `saving(1.gph,replace)` and `saving(2.gph,replace)`, while the data-bearing log remains `all_states_effect_socio_demo.log`, opened with `replace` and then imported. These paths are identical in default and target modes.
findings.why_it_matters: The stated isolation guarantee is incomplete. A target run overwrites the default socio-demographic intermediate, and overlapping default and target runs can read each other's log or graph files, contaminating plotted values despite distinct final PDF names.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n 'saving\(|log using|graph export|file open|save ' CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do` and compare each write path with the `sfx` assignments. The `1.gph`, `2.gph`, and `all_states_effect_socio_demo.log` writes are the unsuffixed exceptions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `sfx` to the socio-demographic log path and to every saved/read `.gph` path, including the `grc1leg` and `graph combine` inputs. Prefer temporary files for the `.gph` intermediates so caller working directories cannot create collisions.

verified_clean.evidence: Both analysis scripts reject any nonempty value other than `mltgt1940` at CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:32-39 and CODE/compute_legibility_quartiles.do:20-26. MATCHING/_figs_tgt_run.do:12-18 captures the inner return code, clears `FIG_NEWLINKS`, and propagates that code.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied. Claims-vs-code review was therefore limited to code comments and output labels; no paper claims were inferred.

The external census and link datasets on D: and F: were not readable in this sandbox, so their actual directory contents, schemas, uniqueness, and target-mode numerical results could not be independently inspected.
The Stata pipeline was not executed. Runtime consequences were inferred from source and Stata semantics; in particular, the batch-log interaction was traced through the runner but not exercised.
The review was scoped to the uncommitted working-tree changes and their immediate link-producing and scoring dependencies, not to the full repository history.
